lpt1_to_file.finding: No. emu2 at commit 9d8698d06e67 has no printer emulation: no BIOS int 17h handler, no LPT port, no LPT1 device name, and DOS handle 4 (PRN) is emu2's own stderr. In QUICK-2, F5 Print on the trapezoid results returns to the shape menu within 0.1 s, writes no file and shows no output.
evidence: emu2 src/dos.c line 87 at the pinned commit

menu_drop_cause.finding: Not a keyboard buffer flush and not a slow start. The title screen is a line input: the first key shows 'Press <Enter> to continue', and typed characters echo there until Enter. A menu digit and Enter sent while the title shows are taken by the title, which is how the spike lost its first two inputs. Keys sent the moment the main menu appears are taken (tried at 0.0, 0.3 and 1.0 s). The main menu is therefore not marked for resend.

frozen_time.finding: Processes in the container see the profile's date (1995-06-01). A fully frozen clock stops emu2's BIOS tick and QUICK-2 hangs on its title screen, so the clock starts at the fixed time on every run and then runs. No date or time has been seen on any QUICK-2 screen so far.

open_questions.question: Harness finding, for a person: 0 at any of the six trapezoid prompts holds the prompt and leaves the screen byte-identical (no message), so no rejected screen can be mapped by marker and every generated case with a 0 waits the full 10 s and times out. Should the runner gain an outcome for 'prompt held' (same prompt and same hash after Enter), and should ranges[*].boundaries keep 0 (and left/right slope min 0) given that 0 is never accepted?
open_questions.answer: Decided by the user: a held prompt (the screen settles unchanged on the same prompt after a form value is sent) ends the case as outcome rejected with no message; the golden names the prompt in held_prompt. 0 stays in the generator's boundaries, because the rebuild has to hold a 0 too. Built in commit 77b5d4f. Live check: left slope 0 on the trapezoid form now ends as rejected, message null, instead of a 10 s timeout. Behaviour cases with their own steps, such as obs-zerohold-000001, are not ended early.

open_questions.question: With Manning's n -1, Begin Calculations leaves the screen unchanged for at least 10 s. Is QUICK-2 hung in its solver, or waiting for a key? What does F7, F2 or a second Enter do from there?

With discharge -1 or slope -1, Begin returns to the shape menu with no message. Why (an error trapped and swallowed?), and are the inputs kept if T is chosen again? The returned shape menu has a stray shadow row on row 0 (hash 0453fe... versus 0f3f15... on first entry); is that the same stray-row effect as design question 5, and does it ever move a field region?

Is the hold rule 'value equals 0' or something wider? Untested: empty Enter, non-numeric text, small values such as .0001 or -.5, and n or slope values that overflow their print field. Only 0, '.000' and -1 were tried.

Harness finding, for a person: a screen of kind 'rejected' (irr_bank_rejected) is identified while a flow waits for its next prompt, but the case does not end there; it times out with message null. Should the flow wait also stop on cases._stop_screens, so a bank-station rejection records as outcome rejected with its message?
open_questions.answer: Decided by the user: a screen the profile marks as rejected or error ends the case where it appears, including during the wait for the next prompt, with the message it printed. Built in commit 77b5d4f: the prompt wait now also stops on the profile's stop screens. Live check: the 40-point section with right bank 255 now ends as outcome rejected on irr_bank_rejected with message 'ERROR! RIGHT Bank Station DOES NOT MATCH a Ground Point. Press <ENTER>' instead of timing out.

open_questions.question: At discharge 8000 on the 40-point section, WS ELEV 12.22 is above the left end point (elevation 12 at station 0) and no warning is shown (Top Wid 386 of a 390 ft section). What does QUICK-2 assume past the end points (vertical walls?), and does it ever warn? Also: what does Enter do after the bank-station ERROR, and is there a limit beyond 40 points (F3 Insert GrPt is not a verified key)?

obs-nodata-000001's later steps (after Begin, F6 and the save prompts) expect irr_editor. nd_irr_result now sits ahead of irr_editor; its marker excludes screens containing 'Enter' or 'Press', which should keep the F6 prompts on irr_editor, but the step right after Begin (keys {F6}) now sees a screen that reads as nd_irr_result. The re-read checks final screens only, so a --replay of obs-nodata-000001 may fail at that step. Does it, and should that control's step expect nd_irr_result?
open_questions.answer: Yes, the replay would have failed there, and the re-read could not see it. The screen right after Begin (screen-20) is a real normal-depth result, so the user chose to make the control's step 21 expect nd_irr_result. The step that saves the file (screen-24, 'SAVING FILE') must stay irr_editor, so nd_irr_result's marker now also excludes 'SAVING FILE'. The re-read now reads the screen each transcript step started from and requires the first match to be the step's expect. Profile version 2; obs-nodata-000001 was rerecorded from the command line, and every golden replays the same (commit 185c4fa).

decisions.saw: Ledger has no decisions or open questions. Design question 1: 6 of 8 cases in batch seed 20261120 timed out, each with a 0 or -1 input. The profile maps no rejected screen for nd_trap_form.
decisions.why: No screen for a rejected input is known, so a case cannot end on one. An interactive session on the trapezoid form shows what the program draws after 0 or -1 at each prompt, which is what a marker would need.

decisions.saw: Session: left slope -1 is accepted, echoed '-1.0', and Begin gives a result screen (depth 4.81, area 59.6, top width 14.8). Batch logs: right slope 0, bottom width 0 and discharge 0 each leave the form hash unchanged after Enter (same prompt, no message); n -1 is accepted, echoed '%-1.0000', and Begin leaves the screen unchanged.
decisions.why: Seven of the twelve 0/-1 combinations are still unseen (left 0, right -1, width -1, n 0, discharge -1, slope 0, slope -1). Probing each prompt in one session is cheaper than a batch that waits 10 s per stuck case. Also need to know whether a stuck prompt takes a valid value afterwards (re-prompt) or hangs.

decisions.saw: Session: 0 holds the prompt with an unchanged screen at left slope, n (both '0' and '.000') and slope; batch logs show the same for right slope, bottom width and discharge. A valid value typed after the held 0 is taken by the same prompt. -1 is accepted at all six prompts; n and slope echo '%-1.0000'. With left 3, right -1, width -1, n .035, discharge -1, slope -1, Begin returned to the shape menu with no message.
decisions.why: A held prompt with no message gives no screen a rejected marker can match, so 0 cannot be mapped as a rejected outcome (harness finding). It can still be cited through a behaviour case with every screen captured; the design requires an exploratory run showing exactly the screens the case expects, so I run the sequence (0 then a valid value at each of the six prompts) in this session first. Note: this entry was written after the T{Enter} that reopened the form, because the first write was refused for a missing op.

decisions.saw: Session 47f8dd7a (no run folder is written for sessions): typing 0 then a valid value at each of the six trapezoid prompts holds each prompt on 0 and takes the valid value; ends on Begin Calculations. -1 is accepted at entry everywhere; left -1 alone gives a result (depth 4.81); n -1 alone stalls at Begin (run 20261121-164750-b814eb); right, width, discharge and slope -1 together return to the shape menu.
decisions.why: What -1 does at Begin is known only for left slope alone and n alone. One exploratory case per remaining input (right, width, discharge, slope at -1, others as nd-trap-000001) separates which input sends the program back to the shape menu. Each case that disproves 'every -1 except n computes' narrows the rule.

decisions.saw: Exploratory, others as nd-trap-000001: right -1 result depth 4.29 (5b1e8f); width -1 result depth 5.04 (4db6bd); left -1 result depth 4.81 (87c871, same as session); n -1 form unchanged after Begin (2917c3, same as batch b814eb); discharge -1 (9da1f1) and slope -1 (ab4f64) return to the shape menu after Begin with no message. 0 at any prompt holds that prompt with an unchanged screen.
decisions.why: The held prompt, the stall on n -1 and the return to the shape menu show no screen a rejected marker could match without also matching normal screens (shape_menu is step 3 of every flow; the held form is identical to the form before the key). So these are mapped as behaviour cases in controls, with every screen captured: obs-zerohold-000001 (0 then a valid value at all six prompts), obs-negreturn-000001 (discharge -1), obs-negreturn-000002 (slope -1), obs-negnstall-000001 (n -1). No new screens; the re-read should pass.

decisions.saw: Profile now holds four new behaviour cases in controls (obs-zerohold-000001, obs-negreturn-000001, obs-negreturn-000002, obs-negnstall-000001). Left slope -1 with nd-trap-000001's other inputs gave depth 4.81 twice (session 47f8dd7a and run 20261121-165631-87c871).
decisions.why: Recording the left -1 case gives the first citable result case and makes the recorder store the four new controls first. If the recorded printed values differ from 87c871, neither is cited.

decisions.saw: nd-trap-000004 (right -1, depth 4.29) and nd-trap-000005 (width -1, depth 5.04) match runs 5b1e8f and 4db6bd on every printed field. title, shape_menu, nd_trap_form, nd_trap_result and the normal_depth/trapezoid flow are still marked unobserved although recorded cases now show each of them.
decisions.why: Design rule 3: a recorded case that shows a screen replaces unobserved with cite. This changes no marker, region or order, so the re-read should pass and the ledger's unobserved list shrinks to what is truly unrecorded.

decisions.saw: Task 2.1 criteria written, citing cases recorded in this run. Design question 2 (irregular section of about 40 points) is untouched; obs-nodata-000001 stores 26 screens of the irregular editor for 4 points, n values .05/.035/.05 and two station-like values 10 and 20.

decisions.saw: obs-nodata-000001 captures: the irregular editor shows 4 STAT/ELEV pairs per row on rows 4-14 (44 slots on one page); after F10 it asks 'Enter  LEFT  Channel Bank Station', then Right, then Manning's n Left, Channel, Right, Discharge, Slope; Enter computes and fills WS ELEV, Area, Top Wid, Hyd R, Flow Type, Chan Vel, Wet Per, Frd #, Depth. The editor shows 'F1 }HELP'.
decisions.why: Whether the editor takes 40 points in a row, how it wraps, and whether bank stations must equal ground-point stations can only be seen by entering them. An interactive session shows each screen before I commit to an 80-step flow.

decisions.saw: Session dd8286a4 (no run folder): 40 points (stations 0 to 390 by 10) entered as station Enter, elevation Enter, four per row on rows 4-13; after the 40th elevation the editor went straight to 'Enter  LEFT  Channel Bank Station' with no F10. Banks 150 and 260 echo as '150.0' and '260.0'. Three n prompts (LEFT, CHANNEL, RIGHT Manning's n Value) echo '0.0600', '0.0350', '0.0800'. With discharge 2500 and slope .002, Enter printed WS ELEV 8.60, Depth 7.1, Area 493, Top Wid 130, Hyd R 3.8, Flow Type SUBCRITICAL, Chan Vel 5.1, Wet Per 131, Frd # 0.46. Prompt texts read from obs-nodata-000001 screens 12-19.

Adding: shape code irr, prompts on irr_editor, a nd_irr_result screen ahead of irr_editor (its marker excludes any screen showing 'Enter' or 'Press', so the F6 and Begin screens stay irr_editor), and a flow with one input step per station and elevation.

decisions.saw: Run 20261121-170823-2e626e through the new normal_depth/irregular flow ended on nd_irr_result with the same printed values as session dd8286a4 (WS ELEV 8.60, Depth 7.1, Area 493, Top Wid 130, Hyd R 3.8, SUBCRITICAL, Chan Vel 5.1, Wet Per 131, Frd # 0.46). The profile re-read passed.
decisions.why: Seen twice; recording gives the citation task 2.2 asks for.

decisions.saw: nd-irr-000001 recorded, identical to run 2e626e. The editor takes three n values (LEFT, CHANNEL, RIGHT) and two bank stations, but at Q 2500 the water (8.60) barely reaches past either bank (7.9 at 150, 8.4 at 260), so a change in an overbank n may not show.
decisions.why: To test 'the overbank n values are used', raise Q to 8000 so both overbanks are wide and wet, then change only n_left to .2, then only n_right to .2. If WS ELEV stays the same the rule is false. Separately, banks 155 and 255 (not ground-point stations) test whether a bank must sit on a ground point.

decisions.saw: Q 8000: base WS ELEV 12.22 (0e0e84); n_left .2 gives 12.52 (88135f); n_right .2 gives 12.37 (35d6ab), so both overbank n values change the answer. Left bank 155 (no ground point at 155) timed out (fb0fd4) on row 24 'ERROR! LEFT Bank Station DOES NOT MATCH a Ground Point.  Press <ENTER>', with the bank fields blank.
decisions.why: This is a real rejection screen with a message, so it can be mapped: screen irr_bank_rejected, kind rejected, marker on 'Bank Station DOES NOT MATCH a Ground Point', message region row 24 col 5 width 71, placed ahead of nd_irr_result and irr_editor (both markers are more general; the result marker already excludes 'Press'). Then the same case should end rejected with that message.

decisions.saw: With irr_bank_rejected mapped, left 155 (3e44a3) and right 255 (6d217d) were both identified as irr_bank_rejected, but each case ran on to wait for the next prompt and timed out, with message null. Right reads 'ERROR! RIGHT Bank Station DOES NOT MATCH a Ground Point. Press <ENTER>'.
decisions.why: The runner does not stop on a rejected screen while waiting for a flow prompt, so these cannot be recorded as rejected outcomes; that is a harness question. They can be cited as behaviour cases ending on irr_bank_rejected: obs-bankreject-000001 (left 155) and obs-bankreject-000002 (right 255), points typed four per step as in session dd8286a4.

decisions.saw: Two bank-rejection behaviour cases added to controls. The Q 8000 runs (0e0e84 base, 88135f n_left .2, 35d6ab n_right .2) were each seen once.
decisions.why: Recording the three Q 8000 cases gives the second sighting and the citation for 'each overbank n changes the answer'. The first call also records the two controls; if either fails to reproduce, the call stores nothing and I learn that before writing any criterion on them.

decisions.saw: nd-irr-000002/3/4 match runs 0e0e84, 88135f, 35d6ab on every printed field. obs-bankreject-000001 and -000002 stored; their last captures show the LEFT and RIGHT ERROR lines, and obs-bankreject-000001 screen-13 shows the LEFT bank prompt right after the 40th point.
decisions.why: Design rule 3: irr_bank_rejected, nd_irr_result, irr_editor and the normal_depth/irregular flow are now shown by recorded cases, so their unobserved notes become cites. No marker, region or order changes.

decisions.saw: Irregular Normal Depth on a 40-point section: seen in session dd8286a4 and runs 2e626e, 0e0e84, 88135f, 35d6ab, fb0fd4, 3e44a3, 6d217d, then recorded as nd-irr-000001..000004 and obs-bankreject-000001..000002 with identical output.
decisions.why: Task 2.2 asks for a cited answer to: does it take separate n for left overbank, channel and right overbank (yes, three prompts, and each overbank n changes WS ELEV), and how are bank stations set (typed as stations after the points; a station with no ground point is rejected). Each criterion has a recorded case and a second sighting.

decisions.saw: Tasks 2.1 and 2.2 are answered with recorded cases: 0 holds each trapezoid prompt; -1 is accepted and computed, stalled or returned depending on the field; the irregular editor takes 40 points, two bank stations that must match ground points, and three n values that each change the answer. Open questions Q-001 and Q-005 need a person's harness decision. Q-002, Q-003, Q-004, Q-006 and Q-007 go past what tasks 2.1 and 2.2 asked, and fit task 3 better than this run. The coverage report's unobserved list predates the last citation-only profile edit (no case has run since), so it still lists irr_editor, nd_irr_result, irr_bank_rejected and flows[normal_depth/irregular], which the profile now cites.

decisions.saw: The answer to Q-007 says a replay of obs-nodata-000001 would have failed under the old profile. That replay was never run. The runner's wait accepts a screen when the expected screen is among the matches, so it would most likely have passed. The gap was in the re-read, which read final screens only.
decisions.why: Correct the record: whether the old replay failed is unknown. The fix stands: under a strict every-step reading, steps 21 and 25 read as nd_irr_result, and both now read as expected.
